focused_question_template: Does the on-path call `{callee_name}` at path position {order} (static definition identity {static_status}; trace callee identity {trace_status}) restrict the resolved filesystem LOCATION to a value the attacker cannot choose, or can attacker influence still determine which file or directory is accessed? Note: a fixed base argument to path.join()/path.resolve() alone does NOT provide containment against '..' traversal -- only an explicit resolve-then-verify-containment check (or equivalent) does.
established_meaning: modeled security property only (attacker controls the resolved filesystem location; not a confirmed path-traversal vulnerability): file permissions, symlink behavior, and actual sensitive-file presence at the resolved location are out of scope for this property
residual_vulnerability_questions: filesystem permissions at the resolved location
presence of a sensitive file actually accessible via attacker-chosen paths
symlink-following and null-byte-injection effects on effective location (explicitly out of scope for v1 -- syntactic/resolved-path control, not filesystem-level effective access)
